output.brief:
Please hold Friday's breach notice. This is not a Tessaly crew problem.

Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crew pool since 1 September, stayed flat at about 3.7 missed bags per 1,000 passengers, and so did Corvane's bags that scanned normally. The entire rise is in bags kicked out to the manual encode desk (about 70 a day in August, about 460 now). That desk backed up, so 91% of the missed ones reached the lateral after the cart closed.

The kick-outs trace to the new Fennick tag stock: those tags fail to scan 11.8% of the time versus 1.5% on Brackwater. Pelion and transfer tags scan normally on every airport reader, so airport equipment is not at fault. On 14–16 October, counters temporarily on Brackwater stock failed at 1.6% while kiosks printing Fennick failed at 12.1%.

Still unknown: whether the Fennick stock is faulty or the printer heat setting needs retuning, and whether the stock causes the printer jams.

Next: switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater now, then test Fennick with adjusted settings before any supplier claim. Confidence in the diagnosis: about 90%.
